territorial_scope.description: Indiana state statute applying to conduct under Indiana criminal law and to Indiana civil limitation periods.

evidence.quote: Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State of Indiana

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Indiana statute that criminalizes distribution of intimate images without the depicted person's consent, including computer-generated or AI-created images, expands voyeurism offences to cover drone use, and sets a longer limitation period for certain child sexual abuse claims against a congressionally chartered organization; most sections take effect July 1, 2024.
summary.long: Amends three Indiana Code provisions and adds a definitions section. Section 1 (effective upon passage) sets limitation periods in IC 34-11-2-4: two years generally; for injury from child sexual abuse, the later of seven years after accrual or four years after the person ceases to be a dependent of the alleged abuser; and a window for claims against a congressionally chartered organization incorporated before June 16, 1916, which may be brought before July 1, 2025 by persons who took part in a specified bankruptcy before January 1, 2024. Section 2 defines terms in IC 34-21.5-2-1, including 'computer generated image' (created or modified by artificial intelligence) and 'intimate image.' Section 3 amends voyeurism in IC 35-45-4-5: voyeurism is a Class B misdemeanor, public voyeurism and remote aerial voyeurism through an unmanned aerial vehicle are Class A misdemeanors, with Level 6 felony tiers for camera use, prior convictions or dissemination. Section 4 amends IC 35-45-4-8 to criminalize distributing an intimate image without consent (Class A misdemeanor; Level 6 felony with a prior conviction), covering AI-created or edited images that appear to depict the victim, and exempting specified distributions, including by news media, cloud service providers, and certain internet providers and search engines. Section 5 declares an emergency.

notes: This is an amending act. Sections 1 to 4 restate each amended section in full, and the text carries no markup showing inserted or struck wording, so changed text cannot be isolated here. The title refers to criminal law and procedure, but Section 1 amends the civil limitation provision IC 34-11-2-4. Two definitions of distribute exist: IC 34-21.5-2-1(3), and IC 35-45-4-8(b), which applies as used in this section and adds posting on a website or application. Section 1 takes effect upon passage, Sections 2 to 4 take effect July 1, 2024, and Section 5 declares an emergency. Passage dates and enactment history are not in the text. Only relations, entities and notes are annotated in this pass.

obligations.summary: Prohibits distributing an intimate image without the depicted individual's consent, where the person knows or should reasonably know there is no consent. Under IC 34-21.5-2-1 and IC 35-45-4-8(c)(2)(C), 'intimate image' includes computer generated or AI-created or modified images, so the prohibition extends to them. Distribution is a Class A misdemeanor, or a Level 6 felony with a prior conviction (penalty recorded under enforcement).

evidence.quote: knows or reasonably should know that an individual depicted in an intimate image does not consent to the distribution of the intimate image

obligations.summary: Prohibits voyeurism: peeping into an occupied dwelling or a place where a person is expected to disrobe without that person's consent, and related conduct under IC 35-45-4-5(b) to (h), including remote aerial voyeurism by unmanned aerial vehicle. Offence grades are recorded under enforcement. The text states the section is amended to read as set out, and the restated text is annotated as provided.
